title: Coherent signed shifts of functorial mapping cocones
statement: Let A be an abelian category, S a category with integer shifts, F,G:S→CochainComplex(A,ℤ) functors with coherent shift isomorphisms, and τ:F→G a natural transformation commuting with shifts. The functor X↦Cone(τ_X)[-1], with diagonal maps of mapping cones, has coherent integer shifts. On the first cocone inclusion its shift map is the shift of F; on the second it is (-1)^m times the shift of G. The formulas include the standard degree-reindexing identifications and hold for all integers m. The shift maps are natural and satisfy the standard zero and successive-shift laws.

source.place: Tag 011G, cochain shifts; derived.tex Tag 014E, mapping cones. Direct signed cocone calculation and Mathlib mappingCone.shiftIso.

proof.text: Use Mathlib mappingCone.shiftIso, shift it by [-1], and interchange [m] and [-1]. Multiply the resulting isomorphism by m.negOnePow. On the cocone inclusions the mapping-cone formulas give coefficient one on the first inclusion and m.negOnePow on the second; m.negOnePow squared is one.

proof.text: Define diagonal cocone maps by homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom followed by [-1]. The inclusion formulas follow from the cofiber map formulas and reindexing. The cocone identity decomposition shows that its two inclusions jointly determine a map out. The arrow-map identity and composition laws define a cocone functor.

source.place: Tag 011G, cochain shifts; derived.tex Tag 014E, mapping cones. Direct signed cocone calculation and Mathlib mappingCone.shiftIso.

proof.text: Apply the diagonal map for the two level shift isomorphisms to the arrow τ, using the shift square of τ, then compose with the signed cocone shift just constructed. The inclusion formulas give the two stated coordinate equations. On each inclusion naturality reduces to naturality of the shift of F or G.

source.place: Tag 011G, cochain shifts; derived.tex Tag 014E, mapping cones. Direct signed cocone calculation and Mathlib mappingCone.shiftIso.

proof.text: Check zero and addition on both inclusions. The first coordinate reduces to the coherence laws for F. The second reduces to those for G and (-1)^(m+n)=(-1)^m(-1)^n. Move the explicit degree-equality isomorphisms across cochains using equality substitution. Package the natural isomorphisms and both coherence equations as CommShift.
